items.title: Added --console flag to claude auth login for Anthropic Console (API billing) authentication

explanation.what_it_is: The --console flag is a new option for the claude auth login command, specifically for Anthropic Console API billing authentication.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows Claude Code users to authenticate with Anthropic Console using the API billing method, which may be required for certain workflows or billing setups.
how_to_use: Use the --console flag with claude auth login to authenticate with Anthropic Console API billing
Example: claude auth login --console

items.title: Added "Show turn duration" toggle to the /config menu

explanation.what_it_is: A toggle in the /config menu that controls the display of turn duration in Claude Code.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature allows users to customize their workflow by choosing whether or not to see turn duration, which can be useful for optimizing conversation flows.
how_to_use: Go to the /config menu and toggle 'Show turn duration' to enable or disable the feature.
Use this toggle to hide turn duration when it's not relevant to your current task, reducing visual clutter.

items.title: [VSCode] Added /remote-control — bridge your session to claude.ai/code to continue from a browser or phone

explanation.what_it_is: The /remote-control command allows you to bridge your current VSCode session to claude.ai/code, enabling continuation of work from a browser or phone.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature matters because it provides flexibility in workflow, allowing Claude Code users to switch between devices and environments seamlessly.
how_to_use: Run the /remote-control command in VSCode to initiate the bridging process
Access your bridged session from a browser by visiting claude.ai/code
Use your phone's browser to continue working on your session from anywhere

items.title: We've added model capability fields to the Models API
items.summary: We've added model capability fields to the Models API. GET /v1/models and GET /v1/models/{model_id} now return max_input_tokens, max_tokens, and a capabilities object. Query the API to discover what…

explanation.what_it_is: The Models API now includes model capability fields, which provide information about the limitations and features of each model, such as max_input_tokens, max_tokens, and a capabilities object.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows Claude Code users to programmatically discover the capabilities of each model, enabling more informed decisions when selecting models for specific tasks.
how_to_use: Use the GET /v1/models endpoint to retrieve a list of models with their corresponding capabilities
Query the GET /v1/models/{model_id} endpoint to get the capabilities of a specific model
Check the capabilities object to determine the supported features and limitations of a model before using it

items.title: Added StopFailure hook event that fires when the turn ends due to an API error (rate limit, auth failure, etc.)

explanation.what_it_is: The StopFailure hook event is a new event in Claude Code that triggers when a turn ends due to an API error, such as rate limiting or authentication failure.
explanation.why_it_matters: This event allows developers to handle and respond to API errors in a more explicit way, enabling better error handling and debugging in their applications.
how_to_use: Use the StopFailure hook to log API error events for debugging purposes
Implement retry logic in response to StopFailure events to handle transient API errors

items.title: Added ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} variable for plugin persistent state that survives plugin updates; /plugin uninstall prompts before deleting it

explanation.what_it_is: The ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} variable allows plugins to store persistent state that remains intact even after plugin updates. This variable enables plugins to retain data across different versions.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update changes how plugins manage data, allowing them to maintain consistency and avoid data loss after updates. It also introduces a prompt before uninstalling a plugin to prevent accidental data deletion.
how_to_use: Use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} to store plugin settings or user preferences that should persist across updates
Access the stored data in your plugin to provide a consistent user experience
Confirm or cancel the uninstallation of a plugin when prompted to avoid unintentionally deleting persistent data

items.title: Added effort, maxTurns, and disallowedTools frontmatter support for plugin-shipped agents

explanation.what_it_is: The effort, maxTurns, and disallowedTools frontmatter options are now supported for agents shipped with plugins, allowing for more fine-grained control over agent behavior.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives developers more flexibility in configuring plugin-shipped agents, enabling them to tailor agent behavior to specific use cases.
how_to_use: Add effort, maxTurns, and disallowedTools options to an agent's frontmatter to customize its behavior
Use these options to limit the number of turns an agent can take or restrict the tools it can use

items.title: Added ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION env var to add a custom entry to the /model picker, with optional _NAME and _DESCRIPTION suffixed vars for display

explanation.what_it_is: The ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION environment variable allows you to add a custom model to the model picker in Claude Code. You can also specify a custom name and description for the model using the _NAME and _DESCRIPTION suffixed variables.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives Claude Code users more flexibility in managing their models, allowing them to easily add and identify custom models. It simplifies the workflow for users who need to work with multiple custom models.
how_to_use: Set the ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION environment variable to the path of your custom model
Optionally, set ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION_NAME and ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION_DESCRIPTION to customize the display name and description of your model

items.title: Added allowRead sandbox filesystem setting to re-allow read access within denyRead regions

explanation.what_it_is: The allowRead sandbox filesystem setting allows read access to specific regions of the filesystem that were previously blocked by denyRead settings.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives Claude Code users more fine-grained control over filesystem access, enabling read operations in areas where they were previously restricted.
how_to_use: Set allowRead to true in your sandbox filesystem configuration to override denyRead settings for specific regions.
Use this setting to enable read access to specific files or directories within a denyRead region.

items.title: We've launched the display field for extended thinking, letting you omit…
items.summary: We've launched the display field for extended thinking, letting you omit thinking content from responses for faster streaming. Set thinking.display: "omitted" to receive thinking blocks with an empty…

explanation.what_it_is: The display field for extended thinking allows you to control whether thinking content is included in responses, with the option to omit it for faster streaming.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change enables faster response times by excluding unnecessary thinking content, which can be beneficial for applications where speed is critical.
how_to_use: Set thinking.display: 'omitted' to receive thinking blocks with empty content
Use this feature to optimize streaming performance in applications with tight latency requirements

items.title: Added MCP elicitation support — MCP servers can now request structured input mid-task via an interactive dialog (form fields or browser URL)

explanation.what_it_is: MCP elicitation support allows MCP servers to request structured input from users mid-task through interactive dialogs, which can be filled out using form fields or by providing a browser URL.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables more dynamic and interactive tasks in Claude Code, as MCP servers can now collect specific information from users at any point during a task.
how_to_use: Use the MCP elicitation support to request user input for tasks that require dynamic data, such as filling out a form or providing a URL for further processing.
Implement interactive dialogs in your MCP servers to collect structured input from users and create more flexible workflows.

items.title: Added new Elicitation and ElicitationResult hooks to intercept and override responses before they're sent back

explanation.what_it_is: New hooks for Elicitation and ElicitationResult that allow interception and override of responses before they are sent back
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives Claude Code users more control over the response pipeline, enabling custom modifications or filtering of responses
how_to_use: Use the Elicitation hook to modify input data before it's processed
Use the ElicitationResult hook to override or transform the response before it's returned to the user

items.title: Added -n / --name <name> CLI flag to set a display name for the session at startup

explanation.what_it_is: The -n or --name CLI flag allows you to specify a custom display name for your Claude Code session when starting up from the command line.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature enables you to easily identify and distinguish between multiple Claude Code sessions running concurrently, making it simpler to manage your workflow.
how_to_use: Use the flag by appending -n or --name followed by your desired session name, e.g., `claude-code -n my_session`
Replace `my_session` with any name that helps you identify the purpose or context of the session

items.title: Added worktree.sparsePaths setting for claude --worktree in large monorepos to check out only the directories you need via git sparse-checkout

explanation.what_it_is: The worktree.sparsePaths setting allows you to specify directories to check out when using claude --worktree in large monorepos, utilizing git sparse-checkout to only retrieve necessary files.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting helps reduce the amount of data that needs to be checked out, making it faster and more efficient to work with large monorepos.
how_to_use: Use the worktree.sparsePaths setting to specify directories to check out, such as 'claude --worktree --sparse-paths=dir1,dir2'
Configure git sparse-checkout to only retrieve necessary files, reducing the amount of data that needs to be checked out

items.title: Added PostCompact hook that fires after compaction completes

explanation.what_it_is: The PostCompact hook is a new event that triggers after the compaction process is complete, allowing for custom actions to be taken after data has been compacted.
explanation.why_it_matters: This hook enables Claude Code users to automate tasks or run custom scripts immediately after compaction, streamlining their workflow and reducing manual intervention.
how_to_use: Use the PostCompact hook to send a notification when compaction is complete
Run a custom script to analyze compacted data
Trigger a data export after compaction

items.title: Added /effort slash command to set model effort level

explanation.what_it_is: The /effort slash command allows you to set the model effort level, controlling the trade-off between response speed and accuracy.
explanation.why_it_matters: This command gives Claude Code users more control over the model's behavior, enabling them to adjust the effort level based on their specific needs and priorities.
how_to_use: Use /effort low to prioritize speed for simple queries
Use /effort medium for a balance between speed and accuracy
Use /effort high for complex queries that require more accurate responses

items.title: Added session quality survey — enterprise admins can configure the sample rate via the feedbackSurveyRate setting

explanation.what_it_is: A session quality survey that collects feedback from users, with a configurable sample rate set by enterprise admins via the feedbackSurveyRate setting.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature allows enterprise admins to gather targeted feedback from users, helping to identify and improve the quality of sessions in Claude Code.
how_to_use: Set the feedbackSurveyRate to a specific percentage, such as 10%, to control how often users are prompted to take the survey.
Use the survey feedback to inform improvements to session quality, such as adjusting settings or optimizing workflows.

items.title: Added actionable suggestions to /context command — identifies context-heavy tools, memory bloat, and capacity warnings with specific optimization tips

explanation.what_it_is: The /context command now provides actionable suggestions to help optimize context-heavy tools, memory bloat, and capacity warnings.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to identify and address performance issues more efficiently, with specific tips for optimization.
how_to_use: Run the /context command to receive suggestions for optimizing context-heavy tools
Use the command to identify memory bloat and receive tips for reducing it
Address capacity warnings with specific optimization recommendations

items.title: Added autoMemoryDirectory setting to configure a custom directory for auto-memory storage

explanation.what_it_is: The autoMemoryDirectory setting allows you to specify a custom directory for storing auto-memory data in Claude Code.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting gives you control over where auto-memory data is stored, which can be useful for managing disk space or organizing project files.
how_to_use: Set autoMemoryDirectory to a custom path in your project settings to store auto-memory data outside the default directory.
Use this setting to keep auto-memory data separate from other project files for easier cleanup or archiving.

items.title: Added modelOverrides setting to map model picker entries to custom provider model IDs (e.g. Bedrock inference profile ARNs)

explanation.what_it_is: The modelOverrides setting allows mapping model picker entries to custom provider model IDs, such as Bedrock inference profile ARNs.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting gives Claude Code users more control over which models are used for inference, enabling more flexibility in their workflows.
how_to_use: Use the modelOverrides setting to map a model picker entry to a specific Bedrock inference profile ARN
Configure the setting to override the default model IDs used by the model picker

items.title: Added actionable guidance when OAuth login or connectivity checks fail due to SSL certificate errors (corporate proxies, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS)

explanation.what_it_is: When OAuth login or connectivity checks fail due to SSL certificate errors, Claude Code now provides actionable guidance to help resolve the issue, particularly in scenarios involving corporate proxies or the NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS environment variable.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update saves users time and effort by providing clear instructions on how to address SSL certificate errors, which can occur when working behind corporate proxies or with custom certificate configurations.
how_to_use: Check the error message for specific guidance on resolving the SSL certificate error
Use the NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS environment variable to specify additional trusted certificates

items.title: Deprecated /output-style command — use /config instead. Output style is now fixed at session start for better prompt caching

explanation.what_it_is: The /output-style command has been deprecated in favor of using /config, and output style is now determined at the start of each session.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change allows for better prompt caching, which can improve performance by reducing the need for repeated computations.
how_to_use: Use the /config command to set output style instead of /output-style
Set output style at the start of each session for optimal caching

items.title: Added w key in /copy to write the focused selection directly to a file, bypassing the clipboard (useful over SSH)

explanation.what_it_is: The w key in the /copy command allows you to write the currently selected text directly to a file, skipping the clipboard. This is done within the Claude Code environment.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature is particularly useful when working over SSH, as it avoids the need to copy and paste between remote and local systems. It streamlines the workflow when you need to save selected text to a file on a remote machine.
how_to_use: Press w while in /copy mode to trigger the file write operation
Use this feature over SSH to save selections directly to remote files

items.title: Added optional description argument to /plan (e.g., /plan fix the auth bug) that enters plan mode and immediately starts

explanation.what_it_is: The /plan command now accepts an optional description argument, allowing you to enter plan mode with a specific task in mind.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update streamlines your workflow by enabling you to start planning a task immediately after invoking the command, without needing to enter a separate description step.
how_to_use: /plan fix the auth bug
/plan refactor the database schema
/plan implement new feature request

items.title: Added claude plugins as an alias for claude plugin

explanation.what_it_is: The 'claude plugins' command is now an alias for 'claude plugin', allowing users to access plugin functionality with either phrase.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change provides an alternative way to interact with plugins, making it easier for users to manage and utilize them within Claude Code.
how_to_use: Use 'claude plugins' to list and manage available plugins
Use 'claude plugins' to install or update a specific plugin

items.title: Added ExitWorktree tool to leave an EnterWorktree session

explanation.what_it_is: The ExitWorktree tool allows you to exit a session that was entered using the EnterWorktree command, returning to the previous workflow state.
explanation.why_it_matters: This addition provides a clear way to exit an EnterWorktree session, making it easier to manage workflow states and avoid potential issues caused by remaining in an unintended state.
how_to_use: Use the ExitWorktree tool to leave an EnterWorktree session when you need to return to the previous workflow state.
Invoke the ExitWorktree command to exit the current EnterWorktree session and resume normal workflow operations.

items.title: Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON environment variable to immediately stop scheduled cron jobs mid-session

explanation.what_it_is: The CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON environment variable allows you to immediately stop scheduled cron jobs in the middle of a session.
explanation.why_it_matters: This variable gives you more control over your cron jobs, enabling you to pause or stop them as needed, even after they've started running.
how_to_use: Set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON to 'true' to stop all scheduled cron jobs mid-session
Use this variable in scenarios where you need to pause or stop cron jobs due to changes in your workflow or environment

items.title: Added support for marketplace git URLs without .git suffix (Azure DevOps, AWS CodeCommit)

explanation.what_it_is: Claude Code now supports Git URLs from Azure DevOps and AWS CodeCommit that do not include the .git suffix, allowing for more flexible repository cloning and management.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update simplifies the process of working with Git repositories from these platforms, as users no longer need to manually append the .git suffix to the URL.
how_to_use: Use the updated Git URL format to clone a repository from Azure DevOps or AWS CodeCommit directly within Claude Code
Update existing repository connections to use the simplified URL format for easier management

items.title: Added /loop command to run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m check the deploy)

explanation.what_it_is: The /loop command allows you to run a prompt or slash command at a specified recurring interval, such as every 5 minutes.
explanation.why_it_matters: This enables Claude Code users to automate repetitive tasks or checks, such as monitoring deployment status, without manual intervention.
how_to_use: /loop 5m check the deploy
/loop 1h run daily report

items.title: Added cron scheduling tools for recurring prompts within a session

explanation.what_it_is: Cron scheduling tools allow you to schedule recurring prompts within a Claude Code session, enabling automated execution of tasks at specified intervals. This feature utilizes cron syntax to define the schedule.
explanation.why_it_matters: With cron scheduling, Claude Code users can automate repetitive tasks, such as data imports or report generation, to run at regular intervals without manual intervention. This streamlines workflows and reduces the need for manual prompting.
how_to_use: Use the cron scheduling tool to schedule a daily prompt to fetch and process new data
Set up a recurring prompt to generate a weekly report at a specified time
Define a cron schedule to automate a task that requires regular execution, such as cleaning up temporary files

items.title: Added voice:pushToTalk keybinding to make the voice activation key rebindable in keybindings.json (default: space) — modifier+letter combos like…

explanation.what_it_is: The voice:pushToTalk keybinding allows you to rebind the voice activation key in Claude Code, which is set to the space bar by default. This keybinding can be customized in the keybindings.json file.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives users more flexibility in choosing a voice activation key that suits their workflow, potentially reducing conflicts with other keyboard shortcuts. Users can now choose modifier+letter combinations as their voice activation key.
how_to_use: Open the keybindings.json file and add a custom keybinding for voice:pushToTalk, such as 'ctrl+shift+v'
Use the default space bar keybinding for voice activation
Experiment with different modifier+letter combinations to find a voice activation key that works best for your workflow

items.title: [VSCode] Added spark icon in VS Code activity bar that lists all Claude Code sessions, with sessions opening as full editors

explanation.what_it_is: A spark icon has been added to the VS Code activity bar, which lists all active Claude Code sessions. These sessions can now be opened as full editors.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows for easier management and access to multiple Claude Code sessions within the VS Code environment. It streamlines workflow by providing a centralized location to view and interact with all sessions.
how_to_use: Click the spark icon in the VS Code activity bar to view a list of all active Claude Code sessions.
Select a session from the list to open it as a full editor in VS Code.

items.title: [VSCode] Added full markdown document view for plans in VS Code, with support for adding comments to provide feedback

explanation.what_it_is: A full markdown document view for plans in VS Code, allowing users to view and interact with plans in a more readable format, and add comments to provide feedback.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to collaborate more effectively on plans within VS Code, by providing a clear and readable view of the plan and allowing for direct feedback.
how_to_use: Open a plan in VS Code to view it in the new markdown document view
Add comments to specific sections of the plan to provide feedback to team members

items.title: [VSCode] Added native MCP server management dialog — use /mcp in the chat panel to enable/disable servers, reconnect, and manage OAuth authentication…

explanation.what_it_is: A native MCP server management dialog in VSCode that can be accessed using the /mcp command in the chat panel, allowing for server management and OAuth authentication.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update streamlines MCP server management within the VSCode environment, eliminating the need to switch between tools or interfaces to manage servers and authentication.
how_to_use: Use /mcp in the chat panel to open the server management dialog
Enable or disable servers directly from the dialog
Reconnect to servers or manage OAuth authentication using the dialog
